name: xmloxide
workload: Criterion benchmarks parsing, serializing, and XPath-querying an Atom feed, SVG drawing, Maven POM, XHTML page, and a 374KB XML document, comparing MiB/s and relative speedups against libxml2
claimed_speedup: Parsing roughly parity to slightly slower than libxml2 (176 vs 184 MiB/s on Atom feed, ~4% slower; 103 vs 92 MiB/s on SVG, 12% faster; 142 vs 148 MiB/s on Maven POM, ~4% slower; 139 vs 157 MiB/s on XHTML, ~13% slower; 169 vs 175 MiB/s on 374KB doc, ~3% slower); serialization 1.5-2.4x faster; XPath evaluation 1.1-2.7x faster (attribute predicates up to 2.7x)
tradeoffs: Pure Rust reimplementation described by its author as 'agent-made' (AI-assisted); not a full libxml2 API-compatible drop-in (has its own MIGRATION.md); benchmark code exists (benches/comparison_bench.rs) but results are mixed, with parsing sometimes slower than libxml2 despite faster serialization and XPath
caveats: No CPU model, compiler, or compiler flags disclosed in README for the published numbers; self-reported by the project; parsing throughput wins are inconsistent (4 of 5 tested docs parse at or below libxml2 speed)
found_via: Hacker News: query "libxml2 replacement" surfaced "Show HN: Xmloxide – an agent-made Rust replacement for libxml2" (HN item 47201816, 64 points)

name: SupXML (sup-xml)
workload: DOM parsing across 21 XML fixtures (7.9KB-95MB) with UTF-8 validation, entity expansion, and tree building under a 'matched contract' harness requiring all parsers under test to perform equivalent validation work; also XSD 1.0 schema compilation/validation against the W3C XSD test suite (14,328 schema tests, 25,092 instance tests)
claimed_speedup: ~2.1x median speedup on full-validation DOM parse across 21 fixtures; ~2.3-2.4x faster XSD schema compilation/validation; example figures cited: a 599KB Arabic text file parses ~3.75x faster, an English Wikipedia article ~2.96x faster; HTML5 parsing only ~1.02x parity with libxml2
tradeoffs: GitHub reports the license as 'Other'/NOASSERTION rather than a recognized OSI license, so the code can be studied but not safely reused despite being public; single-maintainer org with essentially no adoption; ships a drop-in C ABI for libxml2 callers but is a from-scratch Rust reimplementation
caveats: No CPU model, compiler, or flags disclosed; page states numbers come from 'cargo bench -p sup-xml-bench on the checked-in fixture set' but no independent reproduction found; license ambiguity undermines usability despite public benchmark code
found_via: Hacker News: query "Show HN XML parser" / "libxml2 replacement" surfaced "Show HN: SupXML, modern memory-safe XML parser replacement for libxml2" (HN item 48416611) and "SupXML: The modern, memory-safe XML parser drop-in replacement for libxml2" (HN item 48416218)
